sections.title: 2.1 HuggingFace Tokenizers (Very Important)
sections.body:
### Tokenization Process

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               TOKENIZATION PIPELINE                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                            │
│  Raw Text: "Hello, how are you?"                          │
│      │                                                     │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                    │
│  │  1. NORMALIZATION                │                    │
│  │  - Lowercase                     │                    │
│  │  - Unicode normalization         │                    │
│  │  - Strip accents                 │                    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                    │
│      │  "hello, how are you?"                             │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                    │
│  │  2. PRE-TOKENIZATION             │                    │
│  │  - Split on whitespace           │                    │
│  │  - Split on punctuation          │                    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                    │
│      │  ["hello", ",", "how", "are", "you", "?"]         │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                    │
│  │  3. TOKENIZATION MODEL           │                    │
│  │  - BPE / WordPiece / Unigram     │                    │
│  │  - Apply vocabulary              │                    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                    │
│      │  ["hello", ",", "how", "are", "you", "?"]         │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                    │
│  │  4. POST-PROCESSING              │                    │
│  │  - Add special tokens [CLS][SEP] │                    │
│  │  - Create attention masks        │                    │
│  │  - Add token type IDs            │                    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                    │
│      │                                                     │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  Output: {                                                │
│    input_ids: [101, 7592, 1010, 2129, 2024, 2017, ...],  │
│    attention_mask: [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, ...],              │
│    token_type_ids: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, ...]              │
│  }                                                        │
│                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 💡 Example 1: Loading and Exploring Pretrained Tokenizers

```python
# Example 1: Complete tokenizer exploration
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

# Load tokenizer
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

print("🔍 Tokenizer Properties:\n")
print(f"Vocabulary Size: {tokenizer.vocab_size:,}")
print(f"Model Max Length: {tokenizer.model_max_length:,}")
print(f"Tokenizer Class: {type(tokenizer).__name__}")

# Special tokens
print(f"\n🎯 Special Tokens:")
print(f"   PAD: '{tokenizer.pad_token}' (ID: {tokenizer.pad_token_id})")
print(f"   UNK: '{tokenizer.unk_token}' (ID: {tokenizer.unk_token_id})")
print(f"   CLS: '{tokenizer.cls_token}' (ID: {tokenizer.cls_token_id})")
print(f"   SEP: '{tokenizer.sep_token}' (ID: {tokenizer.sep_token_id})")
print(f"   MASK: '{tokenizer.mask_token}' (ID: {tokenizer.mask_token_id})")

# All special tokens
print(f"\n📋 All Special Tokens: {tokenizer.all_special_tokens}")
print(f"📊 Special Token IDs: {tokenizer.all_special_ids}")
```

### 💡 Example 2: Vocabulary and Special Tokens

```python
# Example 2: Working with vocabulary
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

# Accessing vocabulary
vocab = tokenizer.get_vocab()

print(f"📚 Vocabulary Statistics:\n")
print(f"Total Tokens: {len(vocab):,}")

# Show sample tokens
print(f"\n🔤 Sample Vocabulary (first 20):")
for i, (token, idx) in enumerate(list(vocab.items())[:20]):
    print(f"   {idx:5d}: '{token}'")

# Token to ID conversion
print(f"\n🔄 Token ↔ ID Conversion:")
test_tokens = ["hello", "world", "transformer", "##ing"]
for token in test_tokens:
    token_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(token)
    back_to_token = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(token_id)
    print(f"   '{token}' → {token_id} → '{back_to_token}'")

# Check if tokens exist
print(f"\n✅ Token Existence Check:")
check_tokens = ["hello", "xyz123", "artificial", "zzzzz"]
for token in check_tokens:
    exists = token in vocab
    symbol = "✓" if exists else "✗"
    print(f"   {symbol} '{token}': {exists}")
```

### 💡 Example 3: Tokenization, Encoding, and Decoding

```python
# Example 3: Complete tokenization workflow
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

text = "Transformers are revolutionizing Natural Language Processing!"

print(f"📝 Original Text:\n   '{text}'\n")
print("=" * 70)

# Step 1: Tokenization (text → tokens)
tokens = tokenizer.tokenize(text)
print(f"\n1️⃣ TOKENIZATION (text → tokens):")
print(f"   {tokens}")
print(f"   Count: {len(tokens)} tokens")

# Step 2: Encoding (tokens → IDs)
token_ids = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(tokens)
print(f"\n2️⃣ TOKEN IDs (tokens → numbers):")
print(f"   {token_ids}")

# Step 3: Full encoding (with special tokens)
encoded = tokenizer.encode(text)
print(f"\n3️⃣ FULL ENCODING (with [CLS] and [SEP]):")
print(f"   {encoded}")
print(f"   Length: {len(encoded)}")

# Step 4: Decoding (IDs → text)
decoded = tokenizer.decode(encoded)
print(f"\n4️⃣ DECODING (numbers → text):")
print(f"   '{decoded}'")

# Step 5: Decode without special tokens
decoded_clean = tokenizer.decode(encoded, skip_special_tokens=True)
print(f"\n5️⃣ CLEAN DECODING (without special tokens):")
print(f"   '{decoded_clean}'")

# Verify round-trip
print(f"\n✅ Round-trip successful: {text.lower() == decoded_clean.lower()}")
```

### 💡 Example 4: Attention Masks Explained

```python
# Example 4: Understanding attention masks
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

# Different length sentences
texts = [
    "Short text.",
    "This is a medium length sentence.",
    "This is a much longer sentence that contains more information."
]

print("🎭 Attention Masks Visualization\n")
print("=" * 70)

# Encode with padding
encoded = tokenizer(texts, padding=True, return_tensors="pt")

for i, text in enumerate(texts):
    input_ids = encoded['input_ids'][i].tolist()
    attention_mask = encoded['attention_mask'][i].tolist()
    tokens = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(input_ids)
    
    print(f"\n📄 Text {i+1}: '{text}'")
    print(f"   Length: {sum(attention_mask)} real tokens, {len(attention_mask)} total\n")
    
    # Visual representation
    print("   Token         | ID    | Attention")
    print("   " + "-" * 40)
    for token, token_id, mask in zip(tokens, input_ids, attention_mask):
        mask_symbol = "✓" if mask == 1 else "✗"
        token_display = f"{token:13}"
        print(f"   {token_display} | {token_id:5d} | {mask_symbol} {mask}")

print("\n💡 Attention mask = 1: Real token (attend to this)")
print("💡 Attention mask = 0: Padding token (ignore this)")
```

### 💡 Example 5: Truncation and Padding

```python
# Example 5: Truncation and padding strategies
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

long_text = "This is a very long sentence. " * 50  # Very long text
short_text = "Short."

print("✂️ Truncation & Padding Strategies\n")
print("=" * 70)

# Strategy 1: No truncation, no padding
print("\n1️⃣ Default (no truncation, no padding):")
result = tokenizer(short_text)
print(f"   Length: {len(result['input_ids'])}")

# Strategy 2: With padding
print("\n2️⃣ With padding to max_length=20:")
result = tokenizer(short_text, padding='max_length', max_length=20)
print(f"   Length: {len(result['input_ids'])}")
print(f"   Input IDs: {result['input_ids']}")
print(f"   Attention: {result['attention_mask']}")

# Strategy 3: With truncation
print("\n3️⃣ With truncation to max_length=20:")
result = tokenizer(long_text, truncation=True, max_length=20)
print(f"   Original text length: {len(long_text)} chars")
print(f"   Truncated to: {len(result['input_ids'])} tokens")

# Strategy 4: Both padding and truncation
print("\n4️⃣ Multiple texts with padding & truncation:")
texts = [short_text, long_text, "Medium length text here."]
result = tokenizer(texts, padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=20)

for i, text in enumerate(texts):
    real_tokens = sum(result['attention_mask'][i])
    total_tokens = len(result['input_ids'][i])
    print(f"   Text {i+1}: {real_tokens} real / {total_tokens} total tokens")

# Padding strategies comparison
print("\n5️⃣ Padding Strategy Comparison:")
padding_strategies = [
    ('longest', 'Pad to longest sequence in batch'),
    ('max_length', 'Pad to model max length'),
    ('do_not_pad', 'No padding')
]

texts = ["Short", "Medium length", "Very long sentence here"]
for strategy, description in padding_strategies:
    if strategy == 'max_length':
        result = tokenizer(texts, padding=strategy, max_length=15)
    else:
        result = tokenizer(texts, padding=strategy)
    lengths = [len(ids) for ids in result['input_ids']]
    print(f"   {strategy:12}: {lengths} - {description}")
```

### 💡 Example 6: Batch Encoding

```python
# Example 6: Efficient batch encoding
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
import time

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

# Generate test data
texts = [
    "First sentence.",
    "Second sentence is longer than the first.",
    "Third sentence is the longest one in this batch.",
    "Fourth.",
    "Fifth sentence has medium length."
]

print("⚡ Batch Encoding\n")
print("=" * 70)

# Batch encoding
batch_encoded = tokenizer(
    texts,
    padding=True,
    truncation=True,
    max_length=32,
    return_tensors="pt"  # Return PyTorch tensors
)

print(f"\n📦 Batch Encoding Results:")
print(f"   Batch size: {len(texts)}")
print(f"   Tensor shape: {batch_encoded['input_ids'].shape}")
print(f"   (batch_size, sequence_length)\n")

# Show each encoded sentence
for i, text in enumerate(texts):
    input_ids = batch_encoded['input_ids'][i]
    attention_mask = batch_encoded['attention_mask'][i]
    real_tokens = attention_mask.sum().item()
    
    print(f"   Text {i+1}: '{text[:30]}...'")
    print(f"           Real tokens: {real_tokens}, Padding: {len(input_ids) - real_tokens}")

# Compare with individual encoding
print(f"\n⏱️ Performance Comparison (1000 texts):")

# Create more data
large_batch = texts * 200

# Batch encoding
start = time.time()
batch_result = tokenizer(large_batch, padding=True, truncation=True)
batch_time = time.time() - start

# Individual encoding
start = time.time()
individual_results = [tokenizer(text, padding='max_length', truncation=True, max_length=32) for text in large_batch]
individual_time = time.time() - start

print(f"   Batch encoding: {batch_time:.3f}s")
print(f"   Individual encoding: {individual_time:.3f}s")
print(f"   🚀 Speedup: {individual_time/batch_time:.2f}x")
```

### 📝 Exercises - Section 2.1

1. **Exercise 1**: Load 3 different tokenizers (BERT, GPT-2, T5) and compare their vocabulary sizes and special tokens
2. **Exercise 2**: Write a function that finds all tokens in the vocabulary containing a specific substring (e.g., "##ing")
3. **Exercise 3**: Create a visualization showing how the same text is tokenized differently by BERT vs GPT-2
4. **Exercise 4**: Build a padding analyzer that shows padding efficiency (real tokens vs padding tokens) for different strategies
5. **Exercise 5**: Implement a custom function that handles truncation intelligently (keeps beginning and end, removes middle)

sections.title: 2.2 Custom Tokenizers (Advanced)
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Example 1: Train a custom BPE tokenizer
- Initialize tokenizer with BPE model
- Test the trained tokenizer
- Example 2: Train WordPiece tokenizer (BERT-style)
- Domain-specific corpus (medical text example)
- Test with medical terminology
- Example 3: SentencePiece (language-agnostic)
- Note: This example shows the concept, requires sentencepiece package

### Tokenizer Training Process

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           CUSTOM TOKENIZER TRAINING                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                            │
│  Training Corpus                                           │
│      │                                                     │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                    │
│  │  CHOOSE ALGORITHM                │                    │
│  │  • BPE (Byte-Pair Encoding)      │                    │
│  │  • WordPiece                     │                    │
│  │  • Unigram                       │                    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                    │
│      │                                                     │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                    │
│  │  SET HYPERPARAMETERS             │                    │
│  │  • Vocab size                    │                    │
│  │  • Special tokens                │                    │
│  │  • Min frequency                 │                    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                    │
│      │                                                     │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐                    │
│  │  TRAIN ON CORPUS                 │                    │
│  │  Iteratively build vocabulary     │                    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┘                    │
│      │                                                     │
│      ▼                                                     │
│  Custom Tokenizer 🎉                                      │
│                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 💡 Example 1: Training a BPE Tokenizer

```python
# Example 1: Train a custom BPE tokenizer
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import BPE
from tokenizers.trainers import BpeTrainer
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace

# Sample training corpus
training_corpus = [
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
    "Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence.",
    "Natural language processing enables computers to understand human language.",
    "Deep learning models require large amounts of training data.",
    "Transformers have revolutionized natural language processing."
] * 100  # Repeat for better training

print("🔧 Training Custom BPE Tokenizer\n")
print("=" * 70)

# Initialize tokenizer with BPE model
tokenizer = Tokenizer(BPE(unk_token="[UNK]"))
tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()

# Configure trainer
trainer = BpeTrainer(
    vocab_size=1000,
    special_tokens=["[UNK]", "[CLS]", "[SEP]", "[PAD]", "[MASK]"]
)

print("\n⚙️ Training Configuration:")
print(f"   Algorithm: BPE (Byte-Pair Encoding)")
print(f"   Vocab Size: 1000")
print(f"   Training Samples: {len(training_corpus)}")

# Train tokenizer
tokenizer.train_from_iterator(training_corpus, trainer=trainer)

print(f"\n✅ Training Complete!")

# Test the trained tokenizer
test_text = "Machine learning and deep learning are transforming AI."
output = tokenizer.encode(test_text)

print(f"\n🧪 Testing Custom Tokenizer:")
print(f"   Input: '{test_text}'")
print(f"   Tokens: {output.tokens}")
print(f"   IDs: {output.ids}")

# Compare with vocabulary
vocab = tokenizer.get_vocab()
print(f"\n📊 Vocabulary Stats:")
print(f"   Total tokens: {len(vocab)}")
print(f"   Sample tokens: {list(vocab.keys())[:20]}")
```

### 💡 Example 2: Training WordPiece Tokenizer

```python
# Example 2: Train WordPiece tokenizer (BERT-style)
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import WordPiece
from tokenizers.trainers import WordPieceTrainer
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace
from tokenizers.normalizers import Lowercase, NFD, StripAccents
from tokenizers.normalizers import Sequence

# Domain-specific corpus (medical text example)
medical_corpus = [
    "The patient presents with symptoms of hypertension.",
    "Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of mortality.",
    "The diagnosis includes diabetes mellitus type 2.",
    "Pharmaceutical treatment with antihypertensive medications.",
    "Clinical trials demonstrate efficacy of the treatment."
] * 100

print("🏥 Training Domain-Specific WordPiece Tokenizer\n")
print("=" * 70)

# Initialize
tokenizer = Tokenizer(WordPiece(unk_token="[UNK]"))

# Set normalizer (BERT-style)
tokenizer.normalizer = Sequence([NFD(), Lowercase(), StripAccents()])
tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()

# Configure trainer
trainer = WordPieceTrainer(
    vocab_size=2000,
    special_tokens=["[UNK]", "[CLS]", "[SEP]", "[PAD]", "[MASK]"],
    min_frequency=2
)

print("⚙️ Configuration:")
print(f"   Model: WordPiece")
print(f"   Vocab Size: 2000")
print(f"   Domain: Medical text")
print(f"   Normalization: Lowercase + Strip Accents")

# Train
tokenizer.train_from_iterator(medical_corpus, trainer=trainer)

print(f"\n✅ Training Complete!\n")

# Test with medical terminology
test_texts = [
    "Patient diagnosed with hypertension and diabetes.",
    "Cardiovascular complications require pharmaceutical intervention."
]

print("🧪 Testing on Medical Text:")
for text in test_texts:
    output = tokenizer.encode(text)
    print(f"\n   Input: '{text}'")
    print(f"   Tokens: {output.tokens}")
    print(f"   Count: {len(output.tokens)} tokens")
```

### 💡 Example 3: SentencePiece Tokenizer

```python
# Example 3: SentencePiece (language-agnostic)
# Note: This example shows the concept, requires sentencepiece package

print("🌍 SentencePiece Tokenizer\n")
print("=" * 70)

print("""
SentencePiece is a language-agnostic tokenizer that:

✅ Works directly with raw text (no pre-tokenization)
✅ Handles any language (including CJK)
✅ Treats whitespace as normal characters
✅ Supports BPE and Unigram algorithms

Popular in models like:
• T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer)
• XLNet
• ALBERT
• Multilingual models

Training command:
```python
import sentencepiece as spm

spm.SentencePieceTrainer.train(
    input='corpus.txt',
    model_prefix='custom_spm',
    vocab_size=32000,
    character_coverage=0.9995,
    model_type='unigram'  # or 'bpe'
)
```

Loading:
```python
from transformers import T5Tokenizer
tokenizer = T5Tokenizer('custom_spm.model')
```
""")

### 💡 Example 4: Saving and Loading Custom Tokenizer

```python
# Example 4: Save and load custom tokenizers
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import BPE
from tokenizers.trainers import BpeTrainer
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace
import os

print("💾 Saving and Loading Custom Tokenizers\n")
print("=" * 70)

# Train a simple tokenizer
tokenizer = Tokenizer(BPE(unk_token="[UNK]"))
tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()

corpus = ["The quick brown fox"] * 50
trainer = BpeTrainer(vocab_size=500, special_tokens=["[UNK]", "[PAD]"])
tokenizer.train_from_iterator(corpus, trainer=trainer)

# Save tokenizer
save_path = "./custom_tokenizer.json"
tokenizer.save(save_path)
print(f"✅ Tokenizer saved to: {save_path}")

# Check file size
if os.path.exists(save_path):
    size_kb = os.path.getsize(save_path) / 1024
    print(f"   File size: {size_kb:.2f} KB")

# Load tokenizer
print(f"\n📂 Loading tokenizer from disk...")
loaded_tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_file(save_path)
print(f"✅ Tokenizer loaded successfully!")

# Verify it works
test_text = "The quick brown fox jumps"
original_output = tokenizer.encode(test_text)
loaded_output = loaded_tokenizer.encode(test_text)

print(f"\n🔍 Verification:")
print(f"   Original tokens: {original_output.tokens}")
print(f"   Loaded tokens: {loaded_output.tokens}")
print(f"   Match: {original_output.tokens == loaded_output.tokens} ✓")

# Converting to HuggingFace format
print(f"\n🤗 Converting to HuggingFace PreTrainedTokenizerFast:")
from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast

hf_tokenizer = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_object=loaded_tokenizer)
print(f"   Type: {type(hf_tokenizer).__name__}")
print(f"   Vocab size: {len(hf_tokenizer)}")

# Can now use like any HF tokenizer
output = hf_tokenizer(test_text, return_tensors="pt")
print(f"   Compatible with HuggingFace: ✓")

# Cleanup
if os.path.exists(save_path):
    os.remove(save_path)
    print(f"\n🧹 Cleaned up temporary file")
```

### 💡 Example 5: Comparing Tokenization Algorithms

```python
# Example 5: Compare BPE vs WordPiece
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import BPE, WordPiece
from tokenizers.trainers import BpeTrainer, WordPieceTrainer
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace

corpus = [
    "natural language processing",
    "natural language understanding",
    "language models",
    "processing text data",
    "understanding language patterns"
] * 20

test_text = "natural language processing and understanding"

print("⚖️ Comparing Tokenization Algorithms\n")
print("=" * 70)

# Train BPE
bpe_tokenizer = Tokenizer(BPE(unk_token="[UNK]"))
bpe_tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()
bpe_trainer = BpeTrainer(vocab_size=100, special_tokens=["[UNK]"])
bpe_tokenizer.train_from_iterator(corpus, trainer=bpe_trainer)

# Train WordPiece
wp_tokenizer = Tokenizer(WordPiece(unk_token="[UNK]"))
wp_tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()
wp_trainer = WordPieceTrainer(vocab_size=100, special_tokens=["[UNK]"])
wp_tokenizer.train_from_iterator(corpus, trainer=wp_trainer)

# Compare outputs
bpe_output = bpe_tokenizer.encode(test_text)
wp_output = wp_tokenizer.encode(test_text)

print(f"Test Text: '{test_text}'\n")

print("1️⃣ BPE (Byte-Pair Encoding):")
print(f"   Tokens: {bpe_output.tokens}")
print(f"   Count: {len(bpe_output.tokens)}")
print(f"   Method: Merges frequent character pairs\n")

print("2️⃣ WordPiece:")
print(f"   Tokens: {wp_output.tokens}")
print(f"   Count: {len(wp_output.tokens)}")
print(f"   Method: Maximizes language model likelihood\n")

print("📊 Key Differences:")
print("""
BPE:
  ✓ Simpler training algorithm
  ✓ Faster training
  ✓ Used in GPT-2, RoBERTa
  ✗ May create suboptimal splits

WordPiece:
  ✓ Better linguistic splits
  ✓ Uses ## prefix for subwords
  ✓ Used in BERT
  ✗ Slightly slower training
""")
```

2. **Exercise 2**: Compare tokenization efficiency: train tokenizers with different vocab sizes (500, 1000, 5000) and compare average tokens per sentence
3. **Exercise 3**: Build a tokenizer for a programming language (Python code) that preserves code structure
4. **Exercise 4**: Create a multilingual tokenizer trained on mixed language data
